quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: How does the stopping distance for motorcycles compare to cars?

options.text: Cars need much longer to stop.
Cars need a little longer to stop.
Motorcycles need longer to stop.
Motorcycles and cars take about the same amount of time to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles and cars take about the same amount of time to stop.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, motorcycles and cars have nearly the same stopping distance. Wet or slippery pavement makes it much harder for motorcycle riders to stop quickly.

questions.question: Which idea should NOT be used when planning a long group ride?

options.text: Plan travel segments based on the least experienced rider.
Skip breaks so riders reach their destination faster.
Place inexperienced riders behind the leaders.
Ride in a staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Skip breaks so riders reach their destination faster.
questions.explanation: Plan routes based on the least experienced rider. Take regular breaks to reduce fatigue. Place inexperienced riders behind the leader so experienced riders can watch them. Ride in a staggered formation.

questions.question: When a rider bends their left arm at the elbow and points it upward, what does this mean?

options.text: Planning to turn left.
About to stop.
Planning to turn right.
About to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Planning to turn right.
questions.explanation: Riders use hand signals instead of turn signals. A left arm bent at the elbow and pointing upward means the rider plans to turn right or change lanes to the right.

questions.question: To swerve correctly, you should:

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Press the handle grip in the direction you want to swerve.
Press the handle grip in the opposite direction you want to swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handle grip in the direction you want to swerve.
questions.explanation: To avoid a hazard, press the handle grip in the direction you want to go. To swerve left, press the left grip, then the right to straighten. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: Which should you NOT do to prevent fatigue on a long ride?

options.text: Dress warmly.
Limit the distance traveled each day.
Take frequent rest breaks.
Take artificial stimulants.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take artificial stimulants.
questions.explanation: Dress to protect against wind and rain. Ride no more than six hours per day. Take a break at least every two hours. Do not take artificial stimulants because you will experience extreme fatigue when they wear off.

questions.question: Which is a poor reason to sound your horn?

options.text: A driver next to you is too close to the vehicle ahead.
A person is sitting in a parked car.
You want people to notice your motorcycle.
You are passing a person in the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: You want people to notice your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sound your horn before passing a vehicle or pedestrian that might move into your lane. Honk if a driver in an adjacent lane is too close to the car ahead (they may cut in front of you). Honk if someone is in a parked car or if you see a pedestrian or bicyclist in the street.

questions.question: Which portion of the lane should you avoid?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane
No portion should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: No portion should always be avoided.
questions.explanation: There is no lane position that is always best or should always be avoided. Choose your lane position based on current riding conditions.

questions.question: Because of their small size, motorcycles seem to be:

options.text: Traveling faster than they actually are.
Traveling more slowly than they actually are.
Not moving when they actually are.
Closer than they actually are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traveling faster than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Because motorcycles are small, they appear to be going faster than they really are.

questions.question: If one rider in a group wants to go faster than the others, what should the group do?

options.text: Let the rider go ahead and meet at a planned location later.
Speed up to keep everyone together.
Split up and let each rider go their own speed.
Let the faster rider lead the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the rider go ahead and meet at a planned location later.
questions.explanation: If one group member wants to ride faster than the others, let them go ahead and meet up at a designated location later.

questions.question: What happens to face shields and goggles?

options.text: They will never need to be replaced.
They develop scratches and become brittle over time.
They should be made of breakable material that breaks away during a crash.
They should not allow any air to pass through.

questions.correctAnswerText: They develop scratches and become brittle over time.
questions.explanation: Face shields and goggles are made of plastic, which scratches and becomes brittle as it ages. Replace them regularly to stay protected and comfortable.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, all of the following are important except:

options.text: The helmet meets DOT standards.
The helmet looks nice.
The helmet fits snugly.
The helmet has no damage.

questions.correctAnswerText: The helmet looks nice.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT standards for the best protection. It should fit snugly all around and have no damage like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Apply the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Apply the rear brake first, then the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.
Use the brakes in any order.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes together whenever you slow down or stop.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking, you should:

options.text: Release the brake until the rear tire grips the road again, then brake again.
Release the brake and use only the front brake.
Keep the brake locked until the motorcycle stops.
Release the brake and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the brake locked until the motorcycle stops.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while braking, do not release the brake. Keep it locked until you come to a complete stop.

questions.question: To swerve, you should:

options.text: Turn the handlebars quickly.
Move your weight quickly.
Push the handgrip toward the direction you want to turn.
Push the handgrip away from the direction you want to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the handgrip toward the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, push on the handgrip on the side where you want to go. To swerve left, push the left handgrip, then push the right to straighten out. To swerve right, push the right handgrip, then the left.

questions.question: A motorcycle rider can stop other vehicles from sharing their lane by:

options.text: Riding on the left side of the lane.
Riding in the middle of the lane.
Making angry gestures at other drivers.
Riding in a zigzag pattern to take up the whole lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in the middle of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the middle of your lane when other drivers might try to squeeze in next to you. This makes it harder for them to share your lane.

questions.question: A rectangular sign could be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are usually rectangular with white backgrounds and black text. Riders must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: You should not change gears on railroad tracks because:

options.text: Your motorcycle might stall.
You might go too fast.
Other drivers might not expect you to change gears.
The uneven surface makes it harder to shift gears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle might stall.
questions.explanation: Do not shift gears while crossing railroad tracks. Your motorcycle could stall while on the tracks.

questions.question: When riding in a group, you should:

options.text: Never ride in a staggered formation.
Place less experienced riders at the back of the group.
Not use your mirrors.
Not ride too close to other riders in the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not ride too close to other riders in the group.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding. Check your mirrors regularly to watch riders behind you. The leader and last rider should be experienced. Keep proper space between all riders in the group.

questions.question: Swerving a motorcycle:

options.text: Requires a lot of traction.
Requires little traction.
Is a slow maneuver.
Should be done to avoid a hazard on a slippery road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Requires a lot of traction.
questions.explanation: Swerving is a quick move that needs a lot of traction to be safe. Do not swerve suddenly on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: Who should set the speed for a group of riders?

options.text: The leader
The riders just behind the leader
The last rider
The oldest rider

questions.correctAnswerText: The last rider
questions.explanation: The last rider in the group should set the speed. This makes sure no one gets left behind.

questions.question: Eye or face shield protection must have all of these features, except:

options.text: Fastens securely.
Too tight to wear sunglasses or eyeglasses underneath.
Free of scratches.
Allows clear views to both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Too tight to wear sunglasses or eyeglasses underneath.
questions.explanation: Eye or face shields must be free of scratches, resist penetration, allow clear side views, fasten securely, allow air flow to prevent fogging, and have room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: If a dog chases your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Swerve around the animal.
Stop until the animal loses interest.
Ride alongside the animal.
Slow down to approach it, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to approach it, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Downshift and slowly approach the dog. Then accelerate and leave it behind.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When riding through a curve, a group of motorcyclists should:

options.text: Ride in a staggered formation.
Ride in a single-file formation.
Ride in a side-by-side formation.
Use both lanes if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Groups should use single-file formation when going through curves, making turns, entering a highway, or leaving a highway. Staggered formation is used at other times.

questions.question: When loading cargo onto a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Pack heavier items in front of the tank bag.
Pack lighter items near the front.
Try to not place items over the rear axle.
Place items behind the rear axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pack heavier items in front of the tank bag.
questions.explanation: Pack heavier items in front of the tank bag. Place the load over or in front of the rear axle. Putting the load behind the rear axle can affect your control.
